I've farmed this land in Quzhou my whole life. My father grew wheat and corn, and his father before him. I know these two crops. My body isn't what it was — I can't do heavy work like before — so I keep things simple. I farm about 5 mu. My son helps at busy times like harvest and planting, but mostly I manage myself.

Winter wheat goes in after the autumn rains, around October. I buy the improved seed from the village supply station — the kind they push now, Kenong or Jimai variety. I don't fully trust the new hybrid seeds for wheat, improved is fine. I put down compound fertilizer at planting and come back with urea at jointing. Maybe 18 jin of nitrogen total per mu — that's how my neighbor does it and he gets good yield. I flood-irrigate: before winter sets in, again at jointing, at heading, and once more at grain filling. Four times. I spray for powdery mildew and aphids twice.

After wheat harvest in June, I plant summer maize right away on the same land — no-till, straight into the stubble. Hybrid seed, that I trust for corn. Corn I fertilize heavier at planting and side-dress when it's knee-high. Two irrigations if rain is poor. Corn needs less from me in terms of spraying — maybe once or twice for stem borer.

I don't take risks with new crops. I know what the land gives me for wheat and corn. That's what I'll grow.
